title: NodeLinkRAT campaign hides commands in public notepad pages, targets South Korean users
date_note: Genians published the research on Monday 16 November, per Korea JoongAng Daily (published that day); GBHackers reported it on 19 November. The first phishing email in the campaign was dated 12 September 2026 (GBHackers).
actor: Kimsuky (assessed by Genians Security Center, medium confidence)
summary: Genians Security Center said on 16 November that a spear-phishing campaign posed as an aide to a South Korean National Assembly member, Korea JoongAng Daily and GBHackers report. A ZIP held a fake Hangul document shortcut that ran hidden PowerShell and set a scheduled task fetching commands from a public aNotepad page, ending in the NodeLinkRAT remote access tool. Genians assessed Kimsuky may be responsible, with medium confidence, and could not rule out copycats.
plain: Phishing emails posing as a lawmaker's aide install a remote-access tool on Windows PCs, taking its orders from a public notepad web page. Researchers suspect North Korea's Kimsuky.
exec: Command channels on legitimate note sites evade domain blocking.
action: General advice: block or alert on .lnk files inside ZIP attachments, hunt for a scheduled task named CommonMaintenanceHost, and review outbound access to public notepad sites.

sources.name: Korea JoongAng Daily: North Korea-linked hackers suspected of targeting National Assembly seminar attendee

validation.note: Korea JoongAng Daily and GBHackers each report Genians' research and its Kimsuky assessment; Genians' original was not read. aNotepad, the ZIP/LNK chain and the 12 September email date are GBHackers' only; JoongAng says 'a publicly accessible online note-taking service'.

review.note: stronger than the source: plain said researchers link it to Kimsuky, now suspect (Genians medium confidence, may be Kimsuky); rest checked against JoongAng Daily and GBHackers
